title: Keep the four .lore/agents source lists current as bundle concepts are added
description: Measured during the WCLI-24 review (2026-09-28, opum-ai/ward-cli#25): each .lore/agents/*.toml profile declares explicit source lists. Adding a new concept to docs/ (scratch copy: a valid adr/0005-record-format.md with its index link) leaves `lore check --strict` at exit 0, all four pack catalogs unchanged and no warning; the new concept surfaces only as a bundle-wide query hit a specialist must `lore read` by hand. Removal or rename of a referenced id is loud by contrast: `lore agent context` exits 6 with '.lore/agents/<file>.toml references missing concept <id>', `lore check --strict` exits 6, and `lore agent list` errors. So a future ADR that does not touch the four TOMLs is silently absent from every specialist evidence set. Reviewer recommendation: make updating the four source lists part of how an ADR lands here; a Docs-job check (every bundle concept referenced by at least one profile, or explicitly recorded as excluded) is the automating alternative.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A mechanism is decided and recorded (Docs-job check or a recorded ADR-landing step), with the rejected alternative and its reason stated
The chosen mechanism is demonstrated: the current bundle and profiles report clean, and a scratch-added concept is either reported or recorded as a deliberate exclusion

plan: 2. Decide the mechanism (a Docs-job coverage check vs a recorded ADR-landing step) and record it as ADR 0008 with the rejected alternative and its reason.

3. Add scripts/check-lore-agent-sources.mjs: read the bundle concepts from `lore graph --json` and each profile's pinned+sources from `lore agent list/show --json`; fail when a concept is referenced by no profile and is not in the script's explicit exclusion list, and fail rather than pass when it read zero concepts or zero profiles.
4. Reference ADRs 0005-0007 from the profiles that need them, measuring each pack against its max_tokens budget before and after so the fix does not truncate what it means to add.
5. Wire the check into the Docs CI job so the invariant is a required check rather than a convention.
6. Demonstrate, as separate measurements: clean tree green; a scratch-added concept reported by name; the exclusion path green; and the zero-input positive control failing.
7. `lore sync`, `lore check --strict` exit 0, `bun run check` green; independent review over the diff; PR into dev; promote dev to main.
implementationNotes:
MECHANISM DECIDED AND MEASURED (2026-09-29, on feat/WCLI-25-agent-source-coverage). DECISION: a Docs-job check, scripts/check-lore-agent-sources.mjs, fails when a concept in the bundle is a candidate source for no specialist profile unless the check records it as a deliberate exclusion with a reason; the four source lists stay curated by hand. Recorded as ADR 0008 with both rejected alternatives and their reasons -- an ADR-landing convention (nothing watches a convention at the moment it is forgotten, and it cannot express the exclusion half), and extending the check to fail on a truncated pack (the result depends on the task text handed to lore agent context, and it would force budgets to grow with the bundle until the four profiles stopped being different evidence sets). Rejected because the finding is a silent direction, not a missing signal: lore's own checks already fail loudly when a profile names a concept that has gone.

WHAT THE CHECK COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It reads the bundle through lore graph --json and the declared references through lore agent list|show --json, so it holds no second copy of either and cannot drift from them. A declared reference is compared on its concept id, so a heading-qualified entry (id#section) counts. The invariant is "a candidate for at least one profile", deliberately not "every profile": which profile a concept belongs to stays a curation decision the check forces to be made rather than one it makes.

MEASUREMENT 1, CLEAN TREE ACCEPTS: `node scripts/check-lore-agent-sources.mjs` exits 0, "agent source coverage: 9 concepts, 4 profiles, 0 excluded, 0 concepts in no profile". Every Docs-job step re-measured locally through the CLI on PATH at the job's pinned version (lore 0.11.0) rather than through npx: validate --strict 11 files 0 errors 0 warnings, check --strict 11 files 0 errors, agents --check exit 0, and the new step exit 0.

MEASUREMENT 2, THE VIOLATION IS REPORTED: scratched a valid concept in with docs/adr/0009-scratch-probe-concept.md via `lore new adr` plus `lore sync`, so it carried its index link and a log entry exactly as the WCLI-24 review's scratch copy did. Every pre-existing gate stayed at exit 0 over it -- lore check --strict (12 files, 0 errors), lore validate --strict, lore agent list -- and the new check exited 1 naming adr/0009-scratch-probe-concept and telling the reader what to do. That is the finding reproduced end to end, and it is the one measurement the Docs job cannot make for itself: CI only ever sees a clean tree.

MEASUREMENT 3, THE EXCLUSION PATH: with the scratch concept still in the bundle and one entry written into the excluded map, the check exits 0 and prints the exclusion and its reason on the way past, so a concept deliberately in no profile is a visible decision rather than an omission. The map is empty in the landed change.

MEASUREMENT 4, THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRES: the check must fail rather than pass when it read nothing, and does, measured with a stub lore by LORE_BIN. Zero concepts exits 1 "returned 0 concepts; nothing was compared"; zero profiles exits 1 "returned 0 profiles; no source list was read"; a lore that exits 3 with "boom: backend unavailable" exits 1 carrying that message rather than an empty pass.

MEASUREMENT 5, THE TEST SUITE PINS THE REJECT HALF, AND A MUTATION LOCALISES IT: test/lore-agent-sources.test.ts, six cases, all driven through a stub so the Check job can run them (it has bun, not lore). Predicted before running and then measured: replacing the coverage predicate with `false` reddens exactly 1 of 6 -- the case that names that protection -- with the other five green, so the suite tests the properties it names rather than the implementation's identity. Full gate after the change: bun run check exit 0, 368 tests 0 fail (6 new), layer check 0 violations.

WHY THE BUDGETS DID NOT MOVE, WHICH WAS THE OTHER HALF OF THE FINDING. Raising max_tokens until nothing was trimmed was tried first and refuted by measurement. Declaring all seven ADRs against documentation's 10 000 tokens omitted adr/0002, adr/0003 and adr/0004 from a neutral task, with `omitted-by-budget` per source and `truncated: true` on the pack -- at exit 0, which is the same silent-absence shape one layer down. A budget large enough to hold all of them put the pack at 12 363 tokens, i.e. it would have to be raised again the next time a concept landed. What the assembler actually does is narrow by task relevance, measured directly on the review profile: a backup task includes adr/0006-backup-container-and-restore-authority and omits adr/0007-status-and-doctor-reporting, and a status/doctor task does the reverse. So declaring a concept is what makes it reachable and relevance decides whether it arrives, which is what makes a wide candidate set safe and is why every accepted ADR is now a candidate in all four profiles with the budgets untouched.

WHAT WAS NOT CHECKED, stated rather than left to be read as covered: that declaring a concept into a profile is the right profile for it, that a profile's declared set is well chosen, or that a specialist who needs a concept will find it in its pack -- the check catches omission, and curation is still a reading. ADR 0008 is declared in the documentation profile only, deliberately, as the first concept that is not a candidate for every specialist; the check accepts that, which is the demonstration that it asserts reachability rather than uniformity.
